QS: By the time we got to the cinema, the film ____ for ten minutes.
begin 是短暂动作，不能和 for ten minutes 连用；be on 表持续状态，用过去完成时 had been on。
I ____ in this school for three years and I love it here.
考点：现在完成时。for three years 表示从过去持续到现在、并且还在继续，用 have studied；study 是一般现在时，studied 与 for 连用需过去完成或完成时，had studied 表“过去的过去”。
Look! The little boy ____ a picture over there.
考点：现在进行时。Look! 是“此刻正在发生”的信号，主语 the little boy 为单数，故用 is drawing；draws 表习惯、drew 表过去、has drawn 表完成，都与“此刻”冲突。
He ____ to Beijing twice this year.
twice this year 强调到现在的经历，用 have/has been to。
It ____ when we left the house.
考点：过去进行时。when we left 指过去的某一刻，强调那时正在下雨，用 was raining；rains 是一般现在时，has rained 表完成，都与“那一刻”不符。
She ____ her homework when I called her.
考点：过去进行时。when I called 是过去的时间点，从句表示“打电话时她正在做作业”，用 was doing；does/did/has done 都不能表示“正在进行”。
考点：一般现在时的被动语态。教室是动作承受者，且 every day 表习惯，用 is cleaned；cleans 是主动，cleaned 缺 be 动词，is cleaning 表“正在打扫”。
Neither he nor I ____ good at singing.
考点：主谓一致的就近原则。neither…nor 连接主语时，谓语与最近的主语 I 一致，用 am；is/are 与 I 不匹配，be 是原形不能单独作谓语。
The number of students in our school ____ increasing.
考点：主谓一致。the number of + 复数名词意为“……的数量”，中心词是 number，谓语用单数 is；复数意义的是 a number of。
A new library ____ in our town next year.
考点：一般将来时的被动语态。图书馆是“被建造”，且 next year 表将来，用 will be built；will build 是主动，is built 是现在时，builds 时态语态都不对。
Each of the boys ____ a football.
考点：主谓一致。each of + 复数名词作主语时谓语用单数，故选 has；have/are having/were 都是复数或时态不符。
The old man ____ by the police yesterday.
考点：一般过去时的被动语态。老人是“被救”，且有 yesterday，用 was saved；saved 是主动，is saved 是现在时，saves 时态语态都不对。
This is the village ____ I spent my childhood.
考点：定语从句关系副词。从句 I spent my childhood 结构完整，缺的是地点状语，用 where；which/that 不能作状语，when 指时间。
The book ____ cover is red is mine.
考点：whose 引导定语从句。表示“书的封面”，先行词 the book 与 cover 是所属关系，用 whose cover；which/that/who 都不能直接修饰名词。
I don't know ____ he will come tomorrow.
考点：宾语从句引导词。句意为“我不知道他明天是否会来”，表“是否”用 whether；that 无实义，what/which 在从句中要作成分，此处不缺。
____ he said at the meeting surprised us all.
考点：主语从句。从句 he said 缺宾语，用 what 充当 said 的宾语并引导主语从句；that 不作成分，which 表“哪一个”不合语义，it 会造成结构重复。
The reason ____ he was late is that he missed the bus.
考点：定语从句关系副词。the reason 后接 why 引导定语从句，why 在从句中作原因状语；which/that 需在从句中作主语或宾语，此处不缺。
____ you work harder, you will fail the exam.
考点：条件状语从句。句意为“除非你更努力，否则考试会不及格”，用 Unless（= if not）；If 会使逻辑相反，Although/Because 与语义不符。
____ it was raining, we went out for a walk.
考点：让步状语从句。although 引导让步，且英语中 although 与 but 不能同时使用；But/However 会造成双连接，Because 表原因与语义相反。
He is the only person ____ can solve the problem.
考点：定语从句关系代词。先行词 person 指人且在从句中作主语，用 who；whom 只作宾语，which 指物，what 不能引导定语从句。
____ from the top of the hill, the city looks beautiful.
考点：过去分词作状语。逻辑主语 the city 与 see 是被动关系（城市被看），用 Seen；Seeing 表主动，To see 表目的，See 是谓语形式。
He got up early ____ the first bus.
考点：不定式表目的。早起是为了赶上头班车，用 to catch；catching 不作目的状语，caught 是谓语动词，catch 原形不能单独连接。
____ aloud every morning is a good way to learn English.
考点：动名词作主语。句子缺主语，动词作主语要用 -ing，且谓语 is 为单数，用 Reading；Read/Reads 是谓语形式，To reading 搭配错误。
The girl ____ under the tree is my sister.
考点：现在分词作定语。女孩是主动“站”，用 standing 修饰 the girl（相当于 who is standing）；stands 会形成两个谓语，stood 表被动，to stand 不表主动进行。
I'm sorry ____ you waiting for so long.
考点：固定句式 be sorry to do sth。表示“很抱歉让你等这么久”，用 to keep；keep/keeping/kept 都不符合该句式。
Weather ____, we will have a picnic tomorrow.
考点：独立主格结构。Weather 与 permit 是主动关系，且与主句主语 we 不同，用现在分词 permitting；permits 会让句子出现两个谓语。
If I ____ you, I would take the job.
考点：虚拟语气（与现在事实相反）。if 从句用过去式，be 动词一律用 were，故 If I were you；am/had been/be 都不符合该规则。
If he ____ earlier, he would have caught the train.
考点：虚拟语气（与过去事实相反）。主句 would have caught 表明是对过去的假设，从句用 had left；left 是过去式，只用于与现在相反。
I wish I ____ taller than I am.
考点：wish 后的虚拟语气。表示与现在事实相反的愿望，从句用过去式、be 用 were，故 I wish I were taller；am/will be/be 都不表虚拟。
The teacher suggested that we ____ more reading after class.
考点：虚拟语气。suggest 表“建议”时，从句谓语用 (should) + 动词原形，故用 do；did/doing/to do 都不符合该结构。
He talks as if he ____ everything about it.
考点：as if 引导的虚拟语气。与现在事实相反（他并非什么都懂），从句用过去式 knew；knows 是陈述语气，know/be 形式不符。
— Must I finish it today? — No, you ____.
考点：情态动词的问答。Must I…? 的否定回答用 needn't（不必），而不是 mustn't（禁止）；can't 表不可能，shouldn't 表不建议。
The light is on, so he ____ be at home.
考点：情态动词表推测。灯亮着是“有把握的肯定推测”，用 must be；can't be 表否定推测，may not be 语气太弱，needn't 表“不必”。
You ____ have told me earlier; I could have helped you.
考点：情态动词 + have done。should have done 表示“本该做而没做”，含责备；must have done 表肯定推测，can't have done 表否定推测，may have done 表可能。
He ____ swim when he was only five.
考点：情态动词表过去能力。when he was only five 指过去，用 could；can 只表现在能力，may/must 不表能力。
Never ____ I seen such a beautiful place.
考点：部分倒装。否定副词 never 置于句首时，主句要把助动词提到主语前，用 have I seen；had/did 时态不符，was 不能与 seen 搭配。
Only then ____ the importance of health.
考点：only + 状语置于句首的部分倒装。主句需借助助动词 did 并前置，用 did I realize；其余选项均未倒装或时态/结构有误。
It was in 2010 ____ he graduated from college.
考点：强调句。It was … that … 结构中被强调部分是 in 2010，用 that 连接；when/which/where 都不能用于强调句的连接。
So loudly ____ that everyone in the hall could hear him.
考点：so + 副词置于句首的部分倒装。主句用助动词 did 前置，构成 did he speak；其余选项没有倒装。
He is ____ honest boy that everyone likes him.
考点：不定冠词 a/an 的选择。honest 的 h 不发音，读音以元音音素开头，用 an；a 用于辅音音素开头，the 表特指，此处为泛指。
We will meet ____ Monday morning at the school gate.
考点：时间介词。Monday morning 是具体某天的上午，用 on；in 用于月份/年份/季节，at 用于钟点，for 表持续。
Both Tom and Jim ____ interested in music.
考点：主谓一致。both…and 连接两个主语时视为复数，用 are；is/was 是单数，has 不能与 interested 搭配。
Would you like ____ tea before we start?
考点：some 与 any。表示邀请或请求的疑问句用 some，故 Would you like some tea；any 用于纯疑问或否定，a/many 与不可数名词 tea 不搭配。
I prefer tea ____ coffee in the morning.
考点：固定搭配 prefer A to B。比较两物用 to，不用 than；for/with 都不构成该搭配。
考点：比较级的构成。单音节形容词 tall 的比较级是 taller，不能再用 more；more taller 属双重比较，tallest 是最高级。
For the first 15 minutes of my tai chi class, we remain ______ (entire) in one spot to warm up.
考查副词。空处修饰动词 remain，须用副词，entire 的副词形式为 entirely，意为“完全地”。填形容词 entire 不能修饰动词，属词性错误。句意：前十五分钟我们完全待在原地做热身。
Angela, a tai chi ______ (instruct) with twenty-eight years of experience…
考查名词。空前有不定冠词 a，此处指人，即“有 28 年经验的太极教练”，instruct 的名词 instructor 表示“教练、导师”。instruct 是动词，instruction 指“指导、说明”，均不能指人。
考查并列连词。空处连接 mind（头脑）与 body（身体）两个并列名词，表示“身心合一”，故用 and。or 表选择，but 表转折，so 表结果，都与“兼顾身心”的并列关系不符。
考查名词复数。foot 的复数形式为 feet，此处描述“双脚平行”的站姿，需用复数。单数 foot 与“双脚”不符，属忽略语境的形近错误；该句为动作要领，不能用所有格或其他形式。
Now, I ______ (suppose) to feel the weight on my legs.
考查固定搭配与主谓一致。be supposed to do sth. 意为“应该做某事”，全文以一般现在时叙述，主语为 I，故填 am supposed。写成 is supposed 或 supposed 都破坏主谓一致与系动词结构。
We move on to tai chi positions, of ______ there are forty-two.
考查“介词＋关系代词”。先行词是 tai chi positions（事物），介词 of 之后只能用 which 引导非限制性定语从句，that、who 都不能放在介词后，属关系代词的选择错误。
The movements have ______ (describe) names like “holding the bowl”.
考查词性转换。空处修饰名词 names，须用形容词，describe 的形容词 descriptive 意为“描述性的、形象的”，说明招式名字生动。填 description（名词）或 describing 都不合此处修饰名词的需要。
I keep my eyes ______ a woman to my right.
考查固定搭配。keep one's eye on sb./sth. 意为“留意、注视某人或某物”，此处指作者盯着右侧的女士模仿动作，介词只能用 on。用 at、to 等都不构成这一固定短语。
考查非谓语。despite 后接“it being only 8 am”这一独立主格结构，it 与 be 是逻辑上的主谓关系，故用现在分词 being。用 to be 或 be 都不符合 despite 后接名词性结构的用法。
It's time for my dan tian ______ (meet) another life force.
考查固定句型。It's time for sb./sth. to do sth. 意为“到某人或某物做某事的时候了”，应用动词不定式 to meet。用 meeting 或 meet 都破坏该句型的固定结构，属非谓语形式的误选。
In the 18th and 19th centuries, ______ (wealth) people travelled and collected plants, historical objects and works of art.
考点：词性转换。依据：空后是名词 people，需用形容词修饰，wealth 加 y 构成 wealthy“富有的”。排除：wealth 是名词不能作定语，wealthily 是副词，wealthier 为比较级但无比较对象。
They kept their collection at home until it got too big ______ until they died.
考点：并列连词。依据：until it got too big 与 until they died 并列，表示“直到太大或直到去世”两种情形，用 or。排除：and 会让两种情形同时成立，but 表转折、then 表顺承，均不合逻辑。
The 80,000 objects collected by Sir Hans Sloane, for example, ______ (form) the core collection of the British Museum.
考点：时态。依据：主语是 8 万件藏品，空处作谓语，斯隆的收藏与 1759 年开馆都属过去，用一般过去时 formed。排除：forms 现在时、forming 非谓语、have formed 与这一过去时间点不符。
考点：定语从句。依据：先行词 the British Museum 指物，关系词在非限制性从句中作主语，用 which。排除：where 作地点状语，what 不引导定语从句，who 只指人，均可排除。
The parts of a museum open to the public ______ (call) galleries or rooms.
考点：被动语态。依据：主语 the parts of a museum 与 call 是被动关系，且陈述客观事实，用一般现在时被动 are called。排除：call 主动、called 缺助动词、are calling 为进行时，都不合。
Often, only a small part of a museum's collection ______ (be) on display.
考点：主谓一致。依据：主语中心词是 a small part，为单数，谓语用 is。排除：are 用于复数，was 与时间状语 Often 所表的现在时不符，be 是原形不能单独作谓语。
…visitors can imagine ______ (they) living at a different time in history.
考点：反身代词。依据：imagine 的宾语与主语 visitors 同指，用反身代词 themselves，构成 imagine oneself doing。排除：them 是宾格，their 是形容词性物主代词，they 是主格，都不能作宾语。
考点：非谓语动词。依据：空处与前面的 living 并列，同作 imagine 的宾语，故用动名词 walking。排除：walk 原形、to walk 不定式、walked 过去分词都不能与 living 并列作宾语。
Historical ______ (accurate) is important but so is entertainment.
考点：词性转换。依据：空处作主语，前有形容词 Historical 修饰，需用名词 accuracy“准确性”。排除：accurate 是形容词，accurately 是副词，accurateness 虽为名词但罕用且不合此处搭配。
Museums must compete ______ people's spare time.
考点：介词搭配。依据：compete for sth 意为“争夺某物”，此处争夺的是人们的空闲时间与金钱。排除：compete with/against 后接对手，compete in 指参加比赛，都与“争夺时间”不符。
These days, it is not unusual for 10- to 12-year-olds to publish their own websites or for second and third graders ______ (begin) computer classes.
考点：非谓语动词。依据：句中为 it is not unusual for sb. to do sth. 结构，for 后接名词再加不定式，故填 to begin。排除：begin 原形、beginning 分词、began 过去式都不能作 for 的宾语补足成分。
At the same time, computer games are becoming increasingly popular as major publishing houses continue to develop ______ (education) computer programs for children in preschool.
考点：词性转换。依据：空处修饰名词短语 computer programs，需用形容词 educational“教育的”。排除：education 是名词，educating 是动名词，to educate 是不定式，都不能作定语。
Also, technological know-how has become a ______ (require) for most jobs in an increasingly digital world, as the computer has become a common tool in most professions.
考点：词性转换。依据：空前有冠词 a、空后有 for，需填单数名词 requirement“要求”。排除：require 是动词，required 是形容词或过去分词，requirements 是复数与 a 冲突。
Also, technological know-how has become a requirement for most jobs in an increasingly digital world, as the computer has become a common tool in most ______ (profession).
考点：名词单复数。依据：profession 是可数名词，most 后接复数表示“大多数行业”，故用 professions。排除：profession 单数与 most 搭配不当，professional 是形容词，professionally 是副词。
The Digital World is a set of volumes ______ aim to describe how digital systems influence society and help readers understand the nature of digital systems and their many interacting parts.
考点：定语从句。依据：先行词 a set of volumes 指物，关系词在从句中作主语，用 which（也可用 that）。排除：what 不引导定语从句，who 只指人，whose 后须接名词。
Each volume in the set explores ______ wide range of materials, explains the basic concepts of major applications of digital systems, and discusses the influences they have on everyday life.
考点：冠词。依据：a wide range of 是固定搭配，意为“广泛的、大范围的”，故填 a。排除：an 用于元音音素前，the 表特指，some 不能构成这一固定短语。
Each volume in the set explores a wide range of materials, explains the basic concepts of major applications of digital systems, ______ discusses the influences they have on everyday life.
考点：并列连词。依据：句中 explores、explains、discusses 三个谓语并列，用 and 连接。排除：but 表转折、or 表选择、so 表结果，都与并列陈述的语义不符。
Because the number of possible topics ______ (be) practically limitless, we focus on a sample of the most interesting and useful applications and tools and explain the basic principles of technology.
考点：主谓一致。依据：the number of 加复数名词作主语时谓语用单数，且此处陈述客观情况用一般现在时，故填 is。排除：are 用于复数，was 与 were 与全文现在时不一致。
Readers ______ (encourage) to continue exploring the digital world with the guidance of our Further Resources section featured in each volume.
考点：时态和语态。依据：主语 Readers 与 encourage 是被动关系，全文为一般现在时，故用 are encouraged。排除：encourage 是主动，are encouraging 是进行时，encouraged 缺助动词。
Readers are encouraged to continue exploring the digital world with the guidance of ______ (we) Further Resources section featured in each volume.
考点：物主代词。依据：空处修饰名词短语 Further Resources section，需用形容词性物主代词 our。排除：us 是宾格，ours 是名词性物主代词，we 是主格，都不能作定语。
______ is so breathtaking about the experience is the out-of-this-world scenes.
考点：主语从句。空处引导主语从句并在从句中作主语，指“……的事物”，用 What，C 对。That 只起连接作用、不作成分，It 不能引导该从句，Which 表“哪一个”，均不合。
The rolling sea of clouds you see once you are at the top will remind you how tiny we ______ (human) are.
考点：名词单复数。空处作 we 的同位语，主语为复数，须用复数 humans，B 对。human 是单数，humanness 是抽象名词“人性”，humans' 是所有格，都不能作同位语。
It will ______ (undoubted) help you get refreshed!
考点：词性转换。空处修饰动词 help，须用副词作状语，C(undoubtedly)对。undoubted、undoubtable 是形容词，undoubting 是分词，都不能修饰动词 help。
The amazing thing about the spring is that the colder the temperature gets, the ______ (hot) the spring!
考点：比较级。the + 比较级, the + 比较级 表示“越……越……”，故用 hotter，C 对。hot 是原级，hottest 是最高级，hotly 是副词，都不能构成该句式。
Strange, isn't it? But that's how nature is — always leaving us ______ (astonish).
考点：非谓语作宾补。leave sb + 宾补，us 是“感到惊讶”的一方，用 -ed 形容词 astonished，D 对。astonishing 修饰令人惊讶的事物，astonishment 是名词，astonish 是动词。
You can't help wondering how hard it ______ (be) for the people then to put all those rocks into place.
考点：时态与主谓一致。时间状语 then 指过去，主语 it 为单数，用一般过去时 was，B 对。is 时态不符，were 与单数主语不一致，been 不能单独作谓语。
Though it is the only unnatural thing on your way up the mountain, still it highlights the whole adventure ______ offers a place where you can sit down to rest your aching legs.
考点：并列连词。空处连接并列谓语 highlights 与 offers，两者是顺接关系，用 and，B 对。but 表转折，or 表选择，so 表因果，都与“既突出全程又提供歇脚处”的并列不符。
It highlights the whole adventure and offers a place where you can sit down to rest your ______ (ache) legs.
考点：非谓语作定语。ache 与 legs 是主动关系，用现在分词 aching 修饰 legs，C 对。ached 是过去分词，表被动；ache 是原形，aches 是谓语形式，都不能作定语。
As the song goes, this long and winding road will never disappear, and it will always stick in the visitor's memory. It sure does in ______ (I).
考点：名词性物主代词。与 in the visitor's memory 呼应，指 stick in my memory，空后无名词，须用 mine 独立使用，C 对。my 后必须接名词，me 是人称代词，myself 是反身代词。
While you're in China, Mount Huangshan is ______ must to visit!
考点：冠词。must 此处作可数名词，表示“必须做的事”，泛指一件用不定冠词 a，B 对。an 用于元音音素前，the 表特指，one 与 must 搭配不自然。
In the ______ (seven) grade, I started volunteering at the Monterey Bay Aquarium in California.
考点：序数词。表示“七年级”须用序数词 seventh，C 对。seven 是基数词，seventeen、seventy 只是形近数词，都不能修饰 grade 表“第几年级”。
I was upset to learn that many sea animals eat plastic garbage, ______ (think) it is food.
考点：非谓语作状语。think 与主语 many sea animals 是主动关系，用现在分词 thinking 表伴随，C 对。thought 表被动，to think 表目的，think 原形不能作状语。
I decided to do something ______ (educate) people about this problem.
考点：非谓语作目的状语。表示“为了教育人们”用动词不定式 to educate，C 对。educate 原形不能作目的状语，educating 表伴随，education 是名词，均不合。
I decided that if I learned of a company ______ used a lot of plastic, I'd send it an email urging it to cut back.
考点：定语从句。先行词 a company 在从句中作主语，用关系代词 that，A 对。what 不能引导定语从句，who 指人，whose 表所属，均与“公司”这一先行词不合。
I found the contact information of the company ______ emailed its president.
考点：并列连词。“找到联系方式”与“给总裁发邮件”是先后顺承的动作，用 and，C 对。but 表转折，so 表结果，or 表选择，都不合这两个动作的顺承关系。
I told him how ______ (harm) plastic could be to the environment and asked him to consider using more eco-friendly options.
考点：形容词作表语。how harmful plastic could be 中 be 后需形容词，B(harmful)对。harm 是名词或动词，harmfully 是副词，harmed 表被动，都不能作表语。
I was so ______ (excite) when he wrote back to me.
考点：-ed 形容词。主语是 I，表示“感到兴奋”用 excited，B 对。exciting 修饰令人兴奋的事物，excite 是动词，excitement 是名词，都不能作表语。
One of the biggest companies I wrote to ______ (be) Alaska Airlines.
考点：主谓一致与时态。主语 One of the biggest companies 为单数，且叙述过去的事，用 was，B 对。is 时态不符，were 与单数主语不一致，being 不能单独作谓语。
A company ______ (represent) wrote back and told me the airline was switching over from plastic to paper cups on all of its 1,200 daily flights.
考点：名词。指“一位公司代表”，用名词 representative 作同位语，B 对。represent 是动词，representation 是抽象名词，representing 是分词，都不能指人。
A company representative wrote back and told me the airline was switching over ______ plastic to paper cups on all of its 1,200 daily flights.
考点：介词搭配。switch over from A to B 意为“从 A 转换为 B”，空后已有 to，故填 from，C 对。with、for 不合该搭配，to 会与后面的 to 重复。
______ an area about three times the size of Yellowstone National Park, the GPNP will be one of the first national parks in the country.
考点：非谓语动词作状语。句中已有谓语「will be」，空处不能再出现谓语，须用非谓语；cover 与主语 the GPNP 是主动关系（公园占地多少），故用现在分词 Covering。B 项 Cover 为原形、D 项 Covers 为第三人称单数谓语，都会造成一句两谓语；A 项 Covered 表被动，与主动关系不符。
Covering an area about three times ______ size of Yellowstone National Park, the GPNP will be one of the first national parks in the country.
考点：冠词与倍数表达。倍数句型「倍数 + the size of + 名词」中，size 受 of 短语限定，须用定冠词 the。a 表泛指，与「特指黄石公园的面积」矛盾；its 会与后文 of 重复且指代不明；that 是代词，不能直接构成该倍数结构。

The plan will extend protection to a significant number of areas that ______ previously unprotected, bringing many of the existing protected areas for giant pandas under one authority to increase effectiveness and reduce inconsistencies in management.
考点：时态与主谓一致（定语从句）。关系代词 that 指代先行词 areas，为复数；「previously unprotected」表明说的是过去的状态，故用 were。was、is 单复数不符；are 虽是复数，但「previously」要求过去时，属时态错误，是本题最易误选项。

The plan will extend protection to a significant number of areas that were previously unprotected, bringing many of the existing protected areas for giant pandas under one authority ______ effectiveness and reduce inconsistencies in management.
考点：非谓语动词作目的状语。空处与后面的 reduce 并列，共同说明「把保护区统一管理」的目的，须用不定式 to increase（以提高有效性）。increasing 作伴随状语，表同时发生，与「以便」的目的含义不符；increased 是过去分词表被动；increase 原形不能作状语。

The GPNP ______ to reflect the guiding principle of "protecting the authenticity and integrity of natural ecosystems, preserving biological diversity, protecting ecological buffer zones, and leaving behind precious natural assets for future generations".
考点：被动语态与时态。主语 The GPNP 与 design 是被动关系（公园「被设计成」），介绍公园定位用一般现在时，故 is designed。designs 是主动，has designed 是主动完成时，is designing 是主动进行时，三者语态均错，是本题主要干扰。

The GPNP is designed to reflect the guiding principle of "protecting the authenticity and integrity of natural ecosystems, preserving biological diversity, protecting ecological buffer zones, ______ leaving behind precious natural assets for future generations".
考点：并列连词。空前列出 protecting...、preserving...、protecting... 三个并列的动名词短语，最后一项前须用 and 收束这一串列举。but 表转折、or 表选择、so 表结果，都与「逐项列举指导原则」的并列关系不符，填后会使句子逻辑断裂。
The GPNP's main goal is to improve connectivity between separate ______ and homes of giant pandas, and eventually achieve a desired level of population in the wild.
考点：名词单复数。population 在此意为「种群」，是可数名词；空前 separate（不同的）提示不止一个，故用复数 populations。population 单数、populated（动词过去式或形容词）、populating（现在分词）词性均不符，且都无法与 separate 及 homes 并列。
The GPNP's main goal is to improve connectivity between separate populations and homes of giant pandas, and ______ achieve a desired level of population in the wild.
考点：词性转换（副词）。空处修饰动词 achieve，须用副词 eventually（最终）。eventual 是形容词，不能修饰动词；event、events 是名词，更不能作状语，三者都不符合「修饰谓语动词」这一基本要求。
Giant pandas also serve ______ an umbrella species, bringing protection to a host of plants and animals in the southwestern and northwestern parts of China.
考点：固定搭配。serve as 意为「充当、起……作用」，句中「serve ___ an umbrella species」即「作为伞护物种」，故填 as。serve for、serve like、serve with 都不构成这一搭配，其中 like 虽表「像」，但会丢掉「实际起该作用」的含义。
The GPNP is intended to provide stronger protection for all the species ______ live within the Giant Panda Range and significantly improve the health of the ecosystem in the area.
考点：定语从句关系代词。先行词 the species 指物，且被 all 修饰，关系词在从句「___ live within the Giant Panda Range」中作主语，故用 that。who、whom 只能指人；what 不能引导定语从句，是本题最常见的误选。
When he saw a young child hanging from a sixth-floor apartment balcony, Henry ran one hundred metres, jumped over a 1.2-metre fence, and held out his arms to catch the ______ child.
考查非谓语作定语。child 与 fall 是主动、进行的关系，即“正在坠落的孩子”，故用现在分词 falling。fallen 表完成被动，fell 是谓语动词，fall 为原形，均不能作后置定语修饰 child。
______ Brown family live in an apartment building outside Toronto.
考查冠词。the Brown family 特指“布朗一家”，姓氏复数前加定冠词表示某某一家人。a 表泛指，this、that 为指示代词，都不能与 family 构成这一固定指代，属冠词误用。
On the day of the accident, Mrs. Brown was at work and Eric was at home with his father. They both fell ______ while watching TV.
考查固定搭配 fall asleep（睡着）。空处作表语，需用形容词 asleep。sleep 是动词或名词，sleepy 意为“困倦的”但不与 fall 搭配，sleeping 不作此表语，三者均属形近词干扰。
Eric woke up a little later when he heard children playing outside. He pushed a chair onto the balcony, and climbed up ______ them.
考查非谓语表目的。他搬椅子爬上阳台是为了看外面的孩子，不定式 to see 作目的状语。seeing、seen 不表目的；saw 是谓语形式，与前面的 climbed 冲突，破坏句子结构。
When he looked down, he ______ slipped and fell over the edge.
考查词性转换。空处修饰动词 slipped，须用副词。accident 是名词，accidental 是形容词，accidents 是复数名词，只有 accidentally 可作状语，表示“意外地滑了一下”。
He hung on for a few minutes ______ screamed for his father, but his father didn't hear him.
考查并列连词。hung on 与 screamed 是两个先后发生的并列谓语，用 and 连接。so 表结果、but 表转折、or 表选择，都与“坚持了几分钟，又大声呼喊父亲”的顺承关系不符。
Henry ______ his car when he heard the screams.
考查过去进行时。when he heard the screams 指过去某一时刻，此时他“正在修车”，用 was fixing。fixed 表已完成，is fixing 时态不符，has fixed 与过去时间状语矛盾。
He quickly ______ his tools aside, and started running, arms out.
考查动词时态。空处与 started 并列，叙述过去接连发生的动作，须用一般过去时 threw。throw 是原形，thrown 是过去分词，throwing 不能单独作谓语，均属形式干扰。
"He saved my ______ life," Mrs. Brown said.
考查名词所有格。“我儿子的生命”需用 son's 作定语修饰 life。son 不能直接修饰 life，sons 与 sons' 是复数形式，与下文的 my son 单数不一致。
"I don't know ______ to thank him," Mrs. Brown said.
考查“疑问词＋不定式”。句意为“我不知道该如何感谢他”，how to thank him 表示方式。what、who、which 与 thank him 搭配会缺宾语或语义不通，属疑问词的误选。
Xiao long bao (soup dumplings), those amazing constructions of delicate dumpling wrappers encasing ______ soup and sweet, hot food.
考点：词性转换（形容词）。空处与前面的 hot 并列修饰 soup，须用形容词，taste 的形容词为 tasty（美味的）。tasteful 虽也是形容词，但意为「有品位的、格调高的」，不能形容食物味道；taste、tasted、tasting 词性不符，无法并列修饰名词。

To eat one, you have to decide whether ______ a small hole in it first, releasing the steam and risking a spill, or to put the whole dumpling in your mouth, letting the hot soup explode on your tongue.
考点：非谓语动词（whether + 不定式）。空处与后文「or to put the whole dumpling in your mouth」并列，构成 whether to do... or to do... 的选择结构，故用 to bite。biting、bitten、bit 都不能与 whether 连用，也无法与 or to put 保持形式一致。

To eat one, you have to decide whether to bite a small hole in it first, releasing the steam and risking a spill, ______ to put the whole dumpling in your mouth, letting the hot soup explode on your tongue.
考点：并列连词。空前是「whether to bite a small hole... risking a spill」，空后是「to put the whole dumpling in your mouth」，两者是「是先咬个小口，还是整个塞进嘴里」的选择，故用 or。and 表相加、but 表转折、so 表结果，都与 whether...or... 结构不符。
Shanghai may be the ______ home of the soup dumpling, but food historians will actually point you to the neighboring ancient canal town of Nanxiang as xiao long bao's birthplace.
考点：非谓语动词作定语。空处修饰名词 home，home 与 recognize 是被动关系（「被公认的故乡」），故用过去分词 recognized。recognizing 表主动，recognition 是名词，recognize 是动词原形，三者都不能作前置定语修饰 home。
There, you'll find them prepared differently — more dumpling and less soup — and the wrappers are pressed ______ hand rather than rolled.
考点：介词固定搭配。by hand 意为「用手工」，与后半句「rather than rolled」（而不是擀出来的）形成对照。with hand、in hand、on hand 都不表示「手工制作」：in hand 指「在进行中／在手头」，on hand 指「在场、现有」，语义均不合。
Nanxiang aside, the best xiao long bao have a fine skin, allowing them ______ out of the steamer basket without tearing or spilling any of their contents.
考点：非谓语动词＋被动语态。them 指小笼包，与 lift 是被动关系，allow sth to be done 表示「允许某物被……」，故完整答案应为 to be lifted。所给四项中 A 项 to lift 最接近，但严格说漏掉了被动，属选项设置瑕疵；lifting、lifted、lift 都不能用于 allow sb to do 结构。
Nanxiang aside, the best xiao long bao have a fine skin, allowing them to lift out of the steamer basket without tearing or spilling any of ______ contents.
考点：代词。空处修饰名词 contents，须用形容词性物主代词 their，指「小笼包里的汤汁和馅」。them 是宾格，不能作定语；theirs 是名词性物主代词，后面不能再接名词；themselves 是反身代词，与「包子的内容物」这一所属关系不符。
The meat should be fresh with ______ touch of sweetness, and the surrounding soup hot, clear and delicious.
考点：冠词与固定搭配。a touch of 意为「一点点、一丝」，此处修饰不可数名词 sweetness，表示肉馅带一丝甜味。an 只能用于元音音素前，且此处是固定短语；those、these 是复数指示代词，不能修饰 a touch of 这一单数结构。
No matter where I buy them, though, one steamer basket is ______ enough, yet two seems greedy, and so I am always left wanting more next time.
考点：词性转换（副词）。空处修饰形容词 enough，须用副词；rarely enough 意为「几乎从来不够吃」，与后文「yet two seems greedy」形成对照，故填 rarely。rarer、rarest 是比较级和最高级形容词，rarity 是名词，三者都不能修饰 enough。
No matter where I buy them, though, one steamer basket is rarely enough, yet two seems greedy, and so I am always left ______ more next time.
考点：非谓语动词（leave sb doing）。be left doing 表示「处于某种持续状态」，left wanting more 即「总被留在还想再吃的状态」，意为意犹未尽。wanted 表被动，与「我一直想吃」的主动感受不符；want、wants 是谓语形式，不能用在 be left 之后。
Since June 2017, right before the ______ of the two new pandas, Meng Meng and Jiao Qing, I have been helping the panda keepers at the zoo to feel more comfortable and confident speaking English.
考查词性转换。空前有定冠词 the、空后有 of the two new pandas，须填名词，arrive 的名词形式为 arrival；误填 arriving 或原形都不能作 the ... of 结构的中心词。
Since June 2017, right before the arrival of the two new pandas, Meng Meng and Jiao Qing, I have been helping the panda keepers at the zoo to feel more comfortable and ______ speaking English.
考查形容词作表语。and 连接 comfortable 与所填空，二者同作 feel 的表语，须用形容词 confident；confidence 为名词，confidently 为副词，都不能与 comfortable 并列。
And who do they speak English ______?
考查介词。speak English to sb 意为“对某人说英语”，疑问词 who 作介词 to 的宾语被提前，故选 to；of、on、by 与 speak English 搭配均不表“对……说”。
Not the pandas, even though ______ language used for the medical training instructions is actually English.
考查冠词。空后 language 被 used for the medical training instructions 限定，表特指，用定冠词 the；an 用于首次提及的可数名词单数，those、these 不能修饰单数 language。
They talk to the flood of international tourists and to ______ Chinese zookeepers who often come to check on the pandas, which are on loan from China.
考查非谓语作定语。空处修饰 Chinese zookeepers，逻辑上表示“来访的”，用现在分词 visiting 作前置定语；visitor 是名词不能作定语，visits 是谓语形式。
They also need to be ready to give ______ in English with international journalists.
考查名词单复数。give interviews 意为“接受采访”，此处泛指多次采访活动，用复数；interview 单数须加冠词，interviewing、interviewed 为分词，不能作 give 的宾语。
This is ______ they need an English trainer.
考查表语从句。上文说饲养员要用英语接待游客、接受采访，故 This is why they need an English trainer 意为“这就是他们需要英语培训员的原因”；how、when、where 都不能表原因。
So, what are they learning? ______, how to describe a panda's life.
考查副词修饰整句。空处在句首并有逗号，修饰后面 how to describe a panda's life 这一说明，须用副词 Basically；Basic、Basis 为形容词或名词，Basics 为名词复数。
It's been an honor to watch the panda programme develop ______ to see the pandas settle into their new home.
考查并列连词。to watch... 与 (to) see... 两个不定式并列作真正主语，用 and 连接；although、because、unless 引导状语从句，此处并无从句结构。
As a little girl, I ______ to be a zookeeper when I grew up.
考查时态。As a little girl 与 when I grew up 均指童年，叙述过去的愿望用一般过去时 wished；wish 为现在时，wishing 不能作谓语，wishes 与主语 I 不一致。
The latest ______ (engineer) techniques are applied to create this protective functional structure that is also beautiful.
考查名词作定语。空处修饰 techniques，“工程技术”须用名词 engineering 作前置定语；engineer 指“工程师”，engineered 为分词，engineers' 为所有格，均不合。
The latest engineering techniques are applied to create this protective ______ (function) structure that is also beautiful.
考查形容词。空处与 protective 并列修饰 structure，须用形容词 functional，表“功能性的”；function 为名词，functioning 为现在分词，functionally 为副词，都不能直接修饰名词。
These sepals open on warm days ______ (give) the inside plants sunshine and fresh air.
考查非谓语表目的。萼片在温暖的日子张开，目的是让内部植物得到阳光和新鲜空气，用不定式 to give 作目的状语；giving、given 不表目的，give 原形也不能直接作状语。
In cold weather, the structure stays ______ (close) to protect the plants.
考查过去分词作表语。stay 后接形容词或分词表状态，结构“保持关闭”与植物被保护是被动关系，用 closed；close 作形容词意为“近的”，closely 为副词，closing 表主动进行。
Further, the Silk Route Garden around the greenhouse ______ (walk) visitors through a journey influenced by the ancient Silk Road.
考查主谓一致与熟词新义。主语 the Silk Route Garden 为单数，全文用一般现在时介绍建筑功能，谓语填 walks；此处 walk 意为“引领（游客）走过”，walked 时态不符，walking 不能单独作谓语。

Further, the Silk Route Garden around the greenhouse walks visitors through a journey influenced by the ancient Silk Road, by which silk as well as many plant species came to Britain for ______ first time.
考查冠词。for the first time 为固定搭配，意为“首次”，填定冠词 the；a、this、that 都不能构成这一习语，属搭配记忆不牢。
These plants included modern Western ______ (favourite) such as rosemary, lavender and fennel.
考查名词复数。such as 后列举迷迭香、薰衣草、茴香等多种植物，指“现代西方人喜爱的植物”，用复数 favourites；favourite 单数缺冠词，favoured 为分词或形容词，favourite's 为所有格。

The Glasshouse stands ______ a great achievement in contemporary design, to house the plants of the southwestern part of China at the end of a path retracing (追溯) the steps along the Silk Route that brought the plants from their native habitat in Asia to come to define much of the richness of gardening in England.
考查介词。stand as 意为“作为……而存在、堪称”，此处说这座玻璃温室堪称当代设计的杰作；for、like、with 与 stand 搭配均无此义，易因按“作为”之外的汉语思路误填。

The Glasshouse stands as a great achievement in contemporary design, to house the plants of the southwestern part of China at the end of a path retracing (追溯) the steps along the Silk Route ______ brought the plants from their native habitat in Asia to come to define much of the richness of gardening in England.
考查定语从句。先行词 the Silk Route 指物，从句 brought the plants ... 缺主语，用关系代词 that，which 亦可；what 不能引导定语从句，who 指人，where 在从句中只能作状语。

The Glasshouse stands as a great achievement in contemporary design, to house the plants of the southwestern part of China at the end of a path retracing (追溯) the steps along the Silk Route that brought the plants from their native habitat in Asia to come to define much of the ______ (rich) of gardening in England.
考查词性转换。much of the ___ of gardening 中，空处是 of 短语的中心词，需名词 richness，意为“丰富性”；rich 为形容词，richly 为副词，richer 为比较级，均不能作该结构中心词。
Chinese cultural elements commemorating (纪念) Tang Xianzu, ______ is known as “the Shakespeare of Asia,” add an international character to Stratford-upon-Avon, William Shakespeare's hometown.
考点：非限制性定语从句。依据：先行词 Tang Xianzu 指人，从句缺主语，且先行词与从句间有逗号，故用 who。干扰项排除：which 只能指物；that 不引导非限制性定语从句；whom 只能作宾语。
Although they could never have met, there are common ______ (theme) in their works, said Paul Edmondson, head of research for the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust.
考点：名词复数。依据：there are 后须接复数名词，且指两位作家作品中的多个共同主题，故 theme 变为 themes。易错排除：单数 theme 与 are 不一致；themed、theming 是分词形式，不能作从句主语。
Some of the things that Tang was writing about ______ (be) also Shakespeare's concerns.
考点：时态与主谓一致。依据：主语 some of the things 为复数，且所述是四百多年前汤显祖所写内容，属过去事实，故填 were。（部分资料作 are，考场以官方答案 were 为准。）
I happen to know that Tang's play The Peony Pavilion (牡丹亭) is similar in some ways ______ Romeo and Juliet.
考点：介词固定搭配。依据：be similar to sb/sth 意为与……相似，是固定结构，故填 to，此处指《牡丹亭》与《罗密欧与朱丽叶》相似。易错排除：with、for、as 均不能与 be similar 构成该搭配。
Two years later, a six-meter-tall pavilion, ______ (inspire) by The Peony Pavilion, was built at the Firs Garden, just ten minutes' walk from Shakespeare's birthplace.
考点：非谓语动词（过去分词作定语）。依据：pavilion 与 inspire 是被动关系，即“受《牡丹亭》启发而建”，故用过去分词 inspired。干扰项排除：inspiring 表主动，to inspire 表目的或将来，均不合。
Two years later, a six-meter-tall pavilion, inspired by The Peony Pavilion, ______ (build) at the Firs Garden, just ten minutes' walk from Shakespeare's birthplace.
考点：被动语态与一般过去时。依据：主语 a six-meter-tall pavilion 是 build 的承受者，时间状语 Two years later 指过去，故填 was built。易错排除：built 缺助动词，has built 表主动且与过去时间不符。

Those cultural elements have increased Stratford's international ______ (visible), said Edmondson, adding that visitors walking through the Birthplace Garden were often amazed to find the connection between the two great writers.
考点：词性转换（形容词变名词）。依据：形容词 international 后需名词，visible 的名词形式 visibility 意为知名度，故填 visibility。

Those cultural elements have increased Stratford's international visibility, said Edmondson, adding that visitors walking through the Birthplace Garden were often amazed ______ (find) the connection between the two great writers.
考点：固定搭配（不定式）。依据：be amazed to do sth 意为对做某事感到惊讶，故填 to find，表示游客惊讶地发现两位伟大作家之间的联系。易错排除：finding 不能用于该固定搭配，found 则与 be 动词叠加成被动，语义不通。

______ (recall) watching a Chinese opera version of Shakespeare's play Richard II in Shanghai and meeting Chinese actors who came to Stratford a few years ago to perform parts of The Peony Pavilion, Edmondson said, “It was very exciting to hear the Chinese language and see how Tang's play was being performed.”
考点：非谓语动词（现在分词作状语）。依据：句中已有谓语 said，recall 与主语 Edmondson 是主动关系，用现在分词 Recalling 作时间状语，且位于句首需大写。
It was very exciting to hear the Chinese language ______ see how Tang's play was being performed.
考点：并列连词。依据：hear the Chinese language 与 see how Tang's play was being performed 两个不定式并列作真正主语，用 and 连接，构成 it was exciting to do A and do B。易错排除：but 表转折、or 表选择，此处两个动作同为令人兴奋之事，语义并列。
An exhibition at the Jiushi Art Museum in Shanghai is featuring artwork inspired by Go, or weiqi in Chinese, ______ originated in China more than 4,000 years ago.
考点：非限制性定语从句。依据：先行词 Go（围棋）指物，从句缺主语，且先行词与从句间有逗号，故填 which。干扰项排除：that 不引导非限制性定语从句；what 前不能有先行词；where 只作地点状语。
Go is one of ______ earliest binary-based games.
考点：冠词。依据：one of the + 形容词最高级 + 复数名词，earliest 为最高级，故填定冠词 the。易错排除：a、an 不能与最高级连用，this 为指示代词，与复数名词 games 及固定结构都不搭配。
We hope ______ (present) the rather abstract Go game and AI in a visual context, and initiate dialogues with minimalist art, conceptual art and expressionism.
考点：非谓语动词。依据：hope 后接动词不定式，即 hope to do sth，故填 to present，与后面的 initiate 并列作 hope 的宾语。易错排除：presenting 不能作 hope 的宾语；presented 为过去分词，与句意“希望呈现”不符。
You try to lead the opponent into your trap and force them to follow your ______ (guide) till they lose.
考点：词性转换。依据：形容词性物主代词 your 后需名词，guide 的名词形式 guidance 意为引导、指导，且为不可数名词，故填 guidance。易错排除：guide 指“向导”，指人的可数名词，与“跟随你的引导”不符。
The players' personalities ______ (reveal) during the game, and one's weaknesses are exposed to the opponent.
考点：被动语态与主谓一致。依据：主语 personalities 为复数，与 reveal 是被动关系，陈述一般事实，故用一般现在时被动 are revealed。
A decent winner always ______ (try) to beat the opponent by no more than one or two points as a gesture of respect for the other side.
考点：主谓一致与时态。依据：主语 a decent winner 为单数，always 表示习惯性动作，谓语须用第三人称单数 tries。易错排除：try 与单数主语不一致；tried 表过去，is trying 表进行，均与 always 所表的惯常行为不符。
A decent winner always tries (try) to beat the opponent ______ no more than one or two points as a gesture of respect for the other side.
考点：介词搭配。依据：表示以多少分之差获胜用 beat sb by + 数量，故填 by，此处指只赢一两分以示尊重。易错排除：at、in、with 都不能与数量连用表示“领先的差距”。

Tu says that the balance between the black and white pieces, the beauty in the ______ (strategy) placement of the pieces, and the energy flow following each move inspired artists to create oil paintings, sculptures, digitally (digital) generated pictures and silk-screen prints for the exhibition.
考点：词性转换。依据：修饰名词 placement 需形容词，strategy 的形容词为 strategic（或 strategical），故填 strategic。

Tu says that the balance between the black and white pieces, the beauty in the strategic (strategy) placement of the pieces, ______ the energy flow following each move inspired artists to create oil paintings, sculptures, digitally (digital) generated pictures and silk-screen prints for the exhibition.
考点：并列连词。依据：balance、beauty、energy flow 三个并列主语，最后一项前用 and 连接，与前面的逗号构成并列结构。

Tu says that the balance between the black and white pieces, the beauty in the strategic (strategy) placement of the pieces, and the energy flow following each move inspired artists to create oil paintings, sculptures, ______ (digital) generated pictures and silk-screen prints for the exhibition.
考点：词性转换。依据：修饰过去分词 generated 需副词，digital 的副词形式为 digitally，故填 digitally。

Yet now, I live in the countryside of Zhejiang, China with my Chinese husband and his family, ______ bamboo and tea bushes grow wild in the mountains, chickens are always free-range, and central (center) heating doesn't exist.
考点：定语从句。先行词是地点 the countryside，从句成分完整、缺地点状语，故用关系副词 where。which、that 须在从句作主宾，when 指时间，均排除。

Yet now, I live in the countryside of Zhejiang, China with my Chinese husband and his family, where bamboo and tea bushes grow wild in the mountains, chickens are always free-range, and ______ (center) heating doesn't exist.
考点：词性转换。central heating 是固定说法“集中供暖”，需形容词 central 修饰 heating。center 为名词或动词，centered、centrally 都不合该搭配。
Nothing in my life before prepared me ______ this one — and to be sure, the first time I came here I never imagined I would ever feel comfortable in this area.
考点：介词。prepare sb for sth 意为“使某人为……做好准备”。to、with、by 都不能与 prepare sb 构成这一含义，故填 for。
But it's amazing how you can adapt ______ learn in a new environment.
考点：连词。adapt 与 learn 是两个并列的动词原形，用 and 连接表并列。or 表选择、but 表转折、so 表结果，都与“适应并学习”的并列关系不符。
Over time, I've found ______ (I) feeling extremely at home here.
考点：代词。find oneself doing 表示“发现自己处于某种状态”，主语为 I，故用反身代词 myself。me、mine、my 都不能构成该结构。
The “sunshine scent” of freshly sunned clothes ______ (be) one of them.
考点：主谓一致与时态。主语中心词是 the sunshine scent（单数），全文用现在时，故填 is。are 与单数主语不一致，was 与全文时态不符。

Growing up, my family and our neighbors never used clotheslines to dry clothing, denying me the chance ______ (discover) one of the great wonders of sunshine — the sweet “sunshine scent” after sunning clothes for an entire day.
考点：非谓语动词。chance 后接不定式作定语，即 the chance to do sth。discovering、discovered 不能作 chance 的定语，discover 原形亦不成立。
The sun-dried clothes smell especially pleasant where I live, thanks to the ______ (absent) of smog and plenty of blue sky afternoons (afternoon) with lots of fresh air.
考点：词性转换。the ... of 结构需名词，absent 的名词为不可数 absence，此处指“没有雾霾”。absently 是副词，absences 用复数不合不可数用法。
The sun-dried clothes smell especially pleasant where I live, thanks to the absence (absent) of smog and plenty of blue sky ______ (afternoon) with lots of fresh air.
考点：名词的数。plenty of 后接可数名词复数，指“许多个晴朗的下午”，故用 afternoons。单数与 plenty of 不搭，afternoon's、afternoons' 所有格在此无对应中心词。
If you've never experienced the “sunshine scent” from a sheet or shirt ______ (leave) to sun for a day, well, you're missing out on one of life's wonders.
考点：非谓语动词。sheet or shirt 与 leave 是被动关系（被晾在阳光下），用过去分词 left 作后置定语。leaving 表主动，to leave 表目的，均不合被动含义。
It is also common for them ______ (hold) during traditional Chinese holidays such as the Spring Festival and the Mid-Autumn Festival, as well as other local festivals.
考点：非谓语与语态。be common for sb/sth to do 结构，且 them（大集）与 hold 是被动关系，故用不定式被动 to be held。to hold 表主动，holding、held 不能用于该结构。
The exact dates and ______ (frequent) of daji vary from region to region.
考点：词性转换。与 dates 并列作主语须用名词，表“频率”用不可数名词 frequency。frequent 是形容词，frequently 是副词，frequencies 用复数不合不可数用法。
Daji originated from the ancient folk custom of trading goods, which dates back to ______ Han Dynasty.
考点：冠词。朝代名 Han Dynasty 前用定冠词，即 date back to the Han Dynasty。a、one、this 都不能用于朝代名前的特指。
As transportation and communication ______ (be) underdeveloped at that time, it was very difficult for households to obtain daily necessities.
考点：时态与主谓一致。主语是 transportation and communication 两个并列名词，且 at that time 表过去，故用 were。was 与复数主语不一致，is、are 与过去时间矛盾。
As a solution, it was very difficult for households to obtain daily ______ (necessity).
考点：名词的数。daily necessities 是固定搭配“日常必需品”，须用复数。necessity 单数、necessary 形容词、necessarily 副词都不合该搭配。
As a solution, people gathered at specific locations on set days to trade their surplus items ______ what they needed.
考点：介词。trade A for B 意为“用 A 换取 B”，符合以剩余物品换取所需之物的语境。with、to、by 都不能构成“换取”这一含义。
______ (draw) by the aroma of street food, they line up in front of stands that serve steaming dumplings and hot noodle soup.
考点：非谓语动词。they 与 draw 是被动关系（被香味吸引），用过去分词 Drawn 作状语。Drawing 表主动，To draw 表目的，均不合逻辑。
They line up in front of stands ______ serve steaming dumplings and hot noodle soup.
考点：定语从句。先行词 stands 指物，从句缺主语，用关系代词 which。who 指人，whose 表所属，where 作地点状语，均不可。
Before ______ (head) home, they fill their shopping bags with fresh fruit and vegetables from local farmers.
考点：非谓语动词。before 在此为介词，后接动名词 heading home。head 原形、headed 过去分词、to head 不定式都不能作介词宾语。
..., at prices significantly ______ (cheap) than those found in supermarkets.
考点：比较级。句中有 than 表比较，形容词 cheap 须用比较级 cheaper。cheap 为原级、cheapest 为最高级、cheaply 为副词，都不合比较结构。
I have went to the Great Wall twice. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是现在完成时的构成 have + 过去分词。went 是 go 的过去式，过去分词应为 gone；句中已有 have，说明要用完成时，所以错在 went。其余三项 have/to/twice 都不构成错误。
She don't like coffee at all. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是主谓一致与否定助动词。主语 She 为第三人称单数，一般现在时的否定要用 doesn't，不能沿用 don't；likes/coffee 本身没问题。
He is more taller than his brother. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是比较级的构成，属于双重比较错误。taller 已由 tall + -er 构成比较级，不能再加 more；than 引出比较对象，位置正确。
The news are very exciting today. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是不可数名词作主语时的主谓一致。news 虽以 -s 结尾但为不可数名词，谓语要用 is；are 与主语不一致，其余两项无错。
I'm looking forward to see you again. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是固定短语 look forward to 中的 to。此处 to 为介词，后接名词或动名词，故 see 应改为 seeing；looking/forward 构成短语，位置无误。
There is many books on the desk. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是 there be 句型的主语一致。真正主语是 many books（复数），be 动词要用 are；is 与复数主语不一致。
He suggested that we went there by bus. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是虚拟语气在 suggest 后的用法。suggest 表建议时，从句谓语用 (should) + 动词原形，故 went 应改为 go；that/by 无错。
I have been here since three years. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是 since 与 for 的区别。three years 是一段时间，前面用 for；since 后应接时间点（如 since 2020）。have/been 构成完成时，用法正确。
Neither of them have finished the work. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是 neither of + 复数名词作主语时的主谓一致。谓语用单数，故 have 应改为 has；Neither/of/them 本身无误。
The reason why he was late was because he missed the bus. 句子里哪个词用错了？
考点是 the reason is that… 的固定结构。表语从句用 that 引导；because 会与 the reason 语义重复，属常见错误。
How many camps does Pali Overnight Adventures offer this summer?
考点：细节理解。依据：首段写明这是所开设的 17 个夏令营中的 4 个。排除：A、B 把举例的 4 个当成总数，D 把 17 与 4 相加，都是误读数字关系。

Pali Overnight Adventures offers children and teens exciting experiences this summer. From broadcasting to street art, these are just 4 of the 17 highly unique camps being offered.

Broadcasting Camp

Become the next star reporter, news writer, director or producer. While running every aspect of our own news station, kids and their fellow campers will create and host a broadcast airing each night at dinner for the entire camp. Every night it goes on the web, keeping parents and the world informed of the happenings at Pali.

Secret Agent Camp

In the movie Mission Impossible, Tom Cruise made being a secret agent seem like the coolest job ever. Campers who sign up for the 2-week secret agent camp can get to know about the life of real secret agents by learning strategies and military skills on the paintball field.

Culinary Camp

If your child enjoys being in the kitchen, then the culinary camp is definitely the right fit. Campers learn technical skills of roasting, frying and cutting, as well as some recipes that they can take home and share with their families.

Street Art Camp

This camp takes creative license to an entirely new level. Campers will share their colorful ideas and imagination with each other and work together to visualize, sketch and paint with non-traditional techniques to create the coolest mural (壁画) which will be displayed in public for all to see.
What will campers do at the Broadcasting Camp?
考点：细节理解。依据：播音营一段写营员参与新闻台各个环节，制作并主持每晚播出。排除：A 文中只说节目上传网络，并非建站；C 是“成为”记者，D 是晚餐时段播出而非办晚宴。

What was the author's purpose in having the conversation with the students?
考点：目的意图。依据：她先说请把水枪拿给我，再编出“奶奶的箱子”的说法，目的是把违禁物品收走。排除：B 谈孙辈只是借口，C 未推荐玩具，D 与教学法无关。

The end of the school year was in sight and spirits were high. I was back teaching after an absence of 15 years, dealing with the various kinds of “forbidden fruit” that come out of book bags. Now was the spring of the water pistol (手枪).

I decided to think up a method of dealing with forbidden fruit.

“Please bring that pistol to me,” I said. “I'm going to put it in my Grandma's Box.”

“What's that?” they asked.

“It's a large wooden chest full of toys for my grandchildren,” I replied.

“You don't have grandchildren,” someone said.

“I don't now,” I replied. “But someday I will. When I do, my box will be full of wonderful things for them.”

My imaginary Grandma's Box worked like magic that spring, and later. Sometimes students would ask me to describe all the things I had in it. Then I would try to remember the different possessions I supposedly had taken away — since I seldom actually kept them. Usually the offender would appear at the end of the day, and I would return the belonging.

The years went by, and my first grandchild Gordon was born. I shared my joy with that year's class. Then someone said, “Now you can use your Grandma's Box.” From then on, instead of coming to ask their possessions back, the students would say, “That's okay. Put it in your Grandma's Box for Gordon.”

I loved talking about the imaginary box, not only with my students but also with my own children. They enjoyed hearing about all the forbidden fruit I had collected. Then one Christmas I received a surprise gift — a large, beautifully made wooden chest. My son Bruce had made my Grandma's Box a reality.
What do the underlined words “the offender” in paragraph 8 refer to?
The maker of the Grandma's Box.
The owner of the forbidden fruit.
考点：词义指代。依据：空后说“我就把东西还给他”，可见犯规者指违禁物品的主人，即学生。排除：A 家长、B 木箱制作者、C 孙辈都与“归还物品”构不成对应。

The end of the school year was in sight and spirits were high. I was back teaching after an absence of 15 years, dealing with the various kinds of “forbidden fruit” that come out of book bags. Now was the spring of the water pistol (手枪).

I decided to think up a method of dealing with forbidden fruit.

“Please bring that pistol to me,” I said. “I'm going to put it in my Grandma's Box.”

“What's that?” they asked.

“It's a large wooden chest full of toys for my grandchildren,” I replied.

“You don't have grandchildren,” someone said.

“I don't now,” I replied. “But someday I will. When I do, my box will be full of wonderful things for them.”

My imaginary Grandma's Box worked like magic that spring, and later. Sometimes students would ask me to describe all the things I had in it. Then I would try to remember the different possessions I supposedly had taken away — since I seldom actually kept them. What happened to the Golden Gate Bridge on its 50th birthday?
It carried more weight than it could.
It swayed violently in a strong wind.
Its roadway was damaged by vehicles.
Its access was blocked by many people.
考点：细节理解。依据：首段写桥面在“历来被要求承载的最重负荷”下下陷。排除：B 晃动是随后出现的现象，C 路面被车辆损坏、D 通道被人群堵住均无依据。

In May 1987 the Golden Gate Bridge had a 50th birthday party. The bridge was closed to motor traffic so people could enjoy a walk across it. Organizers expected perhaps 50,000 people to show up. Instead, as many as 800,000 crowded the roads to the bridge. By the time 250,000 were on the bridge, engineers noticed something terrible: the roadway was flattening under what turned out to be the heaviest load it had ever been asked to carry. Worse, it was beginning to sway (晃动). The authorities closed access to the bridge and tens of thousands of people made their way back to land. A disaster was avoided.

The story is one of many stories in To Forgive Design: Understanding Failure, a book that is at once a love letter to engineering and a paean (赞歌) to its breakdowns. Its author, Dr. Henry Petroski, has long been writing about disasters. In this book, he includes the loss of the space shuttles (航天飞机) Challenger and Columbia, and the sinking of the Titanic.

Though he acknowledges that engineering works can fail because the person who thought them up or engineered them simply got things wrong, in this book Dr. Petroski widens his view to consider the larger context in which such failures occur. Sometimes devices fail because a good design is constructed with low quality materials incompetently applied. Or perhaps a design works so well that it is adopted elsewhere again and again, with seemingly harmless improvements, until, suddenly, it does not work at all anymore.

Readers will encounter not only stories they have heard before, but some new stories and a moving discussion of the responsibility of the engineer to the public and the ways young engineers can be helped to grasp them.

“Success is success but that is all that it is,” Dr. Petroski writes. It is failure that brings improvement.

考点：细节理解。依据：首段说雨林是药用植物、食物、鸟类和动物的家园，又以蚂蚁和树种数量举例。排除：A 谈氧气在第二段，B 未提面积，C“管理良好”无据。

Rainforests are home to a rich variety of medicinal plants, food, birds and animals. Can you believe that a single bush (灌木丛) in the Amazon may have more species of ants than the whole of Britain? About 480 varieties of trees may be found in just one hectare of rainforest.

Rainforests are the lungs of the planet — storing vast quantities of carbon dioxide and producing a significant amount of the world's oxygen. Rainforests have their own perfect system for ensuring their own survival: the tall trees make a canopy (树冠层) of branches and leaves which protect themselves, smaller plants, and the forest animals from heavy rain, intense dry heat from the sun and strong winds.

Amazingly, the trees grow in such a way that their leaves and branches, although close together, never actually touch those of another tree. Scientists think this is the plants' way to prevent the spread of any tree diseases and make life more difficult for leaf-eating insects like caterpillars. To survive in the forest, animals must climb, jump or fly across the gaps. The ground floor of the forest is not all tangled leaves and bushes, like in films, but is actually fairly clear. It is where dead leaves turn into food for the trees and other forest life.

They are not called rainforests for nothing! Rainforests can generate 75% of their own rain. At least 80 inches of rain a year is normal — and in some areas there may be as much as 430 inches of rain annually. This is real rain — your umbrella may protect you in a shower, but it won't keep you dry if there is a full rainstorm. In just two hours, streams can rise ten to twenty feet. The humidity (湿度) of large rainforests contributes to the formation of rainclouds that may travel to other countries in need of rain.

Jennifer Mauer has needed more willpower than the typical college student to pursue her goal of earning a nursing degree. That willpower bore fruit when Jennifer graduated from University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire and became the first in her large family to earn a bachelor's degree.

Mauer, of Edgar, Wisconsin, grew up on a farm in a family of 10 children. Her dad worked at a job away from the farm, and her mother ran the farm with the kids. After high school, Jennifer attended a local technical college, working to pay her tuition (学费), because there was no extra money set aside for a college education. After graduation, she worked to help her sisters and brothers pay for their schooling.

Jennifer now is married and has three children of her own. She decided to go back to college to advance her career and to be able to better support her family while doing something she loves: nursing. She chose the UW-Eau Claire program at Ministry Saint Joseph's Hospital in Marshfield because she was able to pursue her four-year degree close to home. She could drive to class and be home in the evening to help with her kids.

Jennifer received great support from her family as she worked to earn her degree. Her husband worked two jobs to cover the bills, and her 68-year-old mother helped take care of the children at times.

Through it all, she remained in good academic standing and graduated with honors. Jennifer sacrificed (牺牲) to achieve her goal, giving up many nights with her kids and missing important events to study. “Some nights my heart was breaking to have to pick between my kids and studying for exams or papers,” she says. What made Mr Bissell return to Uzbekistan?
考点：细节理解。依据：第一段写他几年后仍被这个国家吸引，于是重返乌兹别克斯坦写文章。排除：A 文中没有朋友邀请，C 这次并非去教书，D 健康只是他当年离开的原因。

In the mid-1990s, Tom Bissell taught English as a volunteer in Uzbekistan. He left after seven months, physically broken and having lost his mind. A few years later, still attracted to the country, he returned to Uzbekistan to write an article about the disappearance of the Aral Sea.

His visit, however, ended up involving a lot more than that. Hence this book, Chasing the Sea: Lost Among the Ghosts of Empire in Central Asia, which talks about a road trip from Tashkent to Karakalpakstan, where millions of lives have been destroyed by the slow drying up of the sea. It is the story of an American travelling to a strange land, and of the people he meets on his way: Rustam, his translator, a lovely 24-year-old who picked up his colorful English in California, Oleg and Natasha, his hosts in Tashkent, and a string of foreign aid workers.

This is a quick look at life in Uzbekistan, made of friendliness and warmth, but also its darker side of society. In Samarkand, Mr Bissell admires the architectural wonders, while on his way to Bukhara he gets a taste of police methods when suspected of drug dealing. In Ferghana, he attends a mountain funeral (葬礼) followed by a strange drinking party. And in Karakalpakstan, he is saddened by the dust storms, diseases and fishing boats stuck miles from the sea.

Mr Bissell skillfully organizes historical insights and cultural references, making his tale a well-rounded picture of Uzbekistan, seen from Western eyes. His judgment and references are decidedly American, as well as his delicate stomach. As the author explains, this is neither a travel nor a history book, or even a piece of reportage. Whatever it is, the result is a fine and vivid description of the purest of Central Asian traditions.

What is the recent study mainly about?
考点：主旨要义。依据：首段点明同伴的体型与进食习惯会影响我们的进食量，两项实验也都在测进食量。排除：A、B 只是实验的幌子，C 范围过大。

According to a recent study in the Journal of Consumer Research, both the size and consumption habits of our eating companions can influence our food intake. And contrary to existing research that says you should avoid eating with heavier people who order large portions (份), it's the beanpoles with big appetites you really need to avoid.

To test the effect of social influence on eating habits, the researchers conducted two experiments. In the first, 95 undergraduate women were individually invited into a lab to ostensibly (表面上) participate in a study about movie viewership. Before the film began, each woman was asked to help herself to a snack. An actor hired by the researchers grabbed her food first. In her natural state, the actor weighed 105 pounds. But in half the cases she wore a specially designed fat suit which increased her weight to 180 pounds.

Both the fat and thin versions of the actor took a large amount of food. The participants followed suit, taking more food than they normally would have. However, they took significantly more when the actor was thin.

For the second test, in one case the thin actor took two pieces of candy from the snack bowls. In the other case, she took 30 pieces. The results were similar to the first test: the participants followed suit but took significantly more candy when the thin actor took 30 pieces.

The tests show that the social environment is extremely influential when we're making decisions. If this fellow participant is going to eat more, so will I. Call it the “I'll have what she's having” effect. However, we'll adjust the influence. If an overweight person is having a large portion, I'll hold back a bit because I see the results of his eating habits. But if a thin person eats a lot, I'll follow suit. If he can eat much and keep slim, why can't I?

People want to listen to someone who is interesting, relaxed and comfortable. Too often, when you stand up to give a speech, you focus on the “public” at the expense of the “speaking.” (17) Focus on the speaking. Talk directly to your audience, be yourself and make a connection.

Why did the author bring the tiger cubs home?
To let them play with his kids.
考点：细节理解。首段说动物园里三分之一的苏门答腊虎崽活不到成年，故“decided to give them round-the-clock care at home”，A 对。D 只是附带结果，凯南高兴并非动机，B、C 原文无据。

I have worked as a keeper at the National Zoo for 11 years. Spot and Stripe are the first tiger cubs that have ever been born here. Globally, a third of Sumatran cubs in zoos don't make it to adulthood, so I decided to give them round-the-clock care at home.

I've got two children — the younger one, Kynan, was extremely happy about the tigers arriving — but all of us really looked forward to being part of their lives and watching them grow. I wasn't worried about bringing them into my home with my wife and kids. These were cubs. They weighed about 2.5 kg and were so small that there was absolutely no risk.

As they grew more mobile, we let them move freely around the house during the day, but when we were asleep we had to contain them in a large room, otherwise they'd get up to mischief. We'd come down in the morning to find they'd turned the room upside down, and left it looking like a zoo.

Things quickly got very intense due to the huge amount of energy required to look after them. There were some tough times and I just felt extremely tired. I was grateful that my family was there to help. We had to have a bit of a production line going, making up 'tiger milk', washing baby bottles, and cleaning the floors.

When Spot and Stripe were four months old, they were learning how to open doors and jump fences, and we knew it really was time for them to go. It was hard for us to finally part with them. For the first few days, Kynan was always a bit disappointed that the cubs weren't there.

I'm not sad about it. I'm hands-on with them every day at the zoo, and I do look back very fondly on the time that we had them.

What will Zafirakou do with her prize money?
考点：细节理解。第二段“I've started a project to promote the teaching of the arts in our schools”，首段也说奖金用于把励志人物请进校园，C 对。A 把“movie star”误读为拍电影，B、D 均非奖金用途。

A British woman who won a $1 million prize after she was named the World's Best Teacher will use the cash to bring inspirational figures into UK schools.

Andria Zafirakou, a north London secondary school teacher, said she wanted to bring about a classroom revolution. 'We are going to make a change,' she said. 'I've started a project to promote the teaching of the arts in our schools.'

The project results from the difficulties many schools have in getting artists of any sort — whether an up-and-coming local musician or a major movie star — into schools to work with and inspire children.

Zafirakou began the project at Alperton Community School, her place of work for the past twelve years. 'I've seen those magic moments when children are talking to someone they are inspired by — their eyes are shining and their faces light up,' she said. 'We need artists more than ever in our schools.'

Artist Michael Craig-Martin said: 'Andria's brilliant project to bring artists from all fields into direct contact with children is particularly welcome at a time when the arts are being downgraded in schools.' It was a mistake to see the arts as unnecessary, he added.

Historian Sir Simon Schama is also a supporter of the project. He said that arts education in schools was not just an add-on.

'It is absolutely necessary. The future depends on creativity and creativity depends on the young. What will remain of us when artificial intelligence takes over will be our creativity, and it is our creative spirit, our visionary sense of freshness, that has been our strength for centuries.'
What does Craig-Martin think of the teaching of the arts in UK schools?
考点：观点态度。他说在学校艺术被“downgraded”时该项目“particularly welcome”，又称视艺术为不必要是“mistake”，可见他认为艺术教育应更受重视，D 对。A 把“难请艺术家”移花接木，B、C 非其观点。

An Australian professor is developing a robot to monitor the health of grazing cattle, a development that could bring big changes to a profession that's relied largely on a low-tech approach for decades but is facing a labor shortage.

Salah Sukkarieh, a professor at the University of Sydney, sees robots as necessary given how cattlemen are aging. He is building a four-wheeled robot that will run on solar and electric power. It will use cameras and sensors to monitor the animals. A computer system will analyze the video to determine whether a cow is sick. Radio tags on the animals will measure temperature changes. The quality of grassland will be tracked by monitoring the shape, color and texture of grass. That way, cattlemen will know whether they need to move their cattle to another field for nutrition purposes.

Machines have largely taken over planting, watering and harvesting crops such as corn and wheat, but the monitoring of cattle has gone through fewer changes.

For Texas cattleman Pete Bonds, it's increasingly difficult to find workers interested in watching cattle. But Bonds doesn't believe a robot is right for the job. Years of experience in the industry — and failed attempts to use technology — have convinced him that the best way to check cattle is with a man on a horse. Bonds, who bought his first cattle almost 50 years ago, still has each of his cowboys inspect 300 or 400 cattle daily and look for signs that an animal is getting sick.

Other cattlemen see more promise in robots. Michael Kelsey, vice president of the Oklahoma Cattlemen's Association, said a robot could be extremely useful given rising concerns about cattle theft. Cattle tend to be kept in remote places and their value has risen, making them appealing targets.
What will Sukkarieh's robot be able to do?
考点：细节理解。第二段“The quality of grassland will be tracked by monitoring the shape, color and texture of grass”，A 对。机器人只判断牛是否生病而不治病，B 错；C 是它提供信息、由人决定，D 原文未提。

What should Titterman be able to do to be a page turner?
考点：细节理解。第一段引语“I'm not a trained musician, but I've learnt to read music so I can help Maria”，说明他靠读谱胜任，A 对。B 与“没受过专业音乐训练”矛盾，C、D 原文无据，属臆造。

By day, Robert Titterman is a lawyer. In his spare time though he goes on stage beside pianist Maria Raspopova — not as a musician but as her page turner. 'I'm not a trained musician, but I've learnt to read music so I can help Maria in her performance.'

Mr Titterman is chairman of the Omega Ensemble but has been the group's official page turner for the past four years. His job is to sit beside the pianist and turn the pages of the score so the musician doesn't have to break the flow of sound by doing it themselves. He said he became just as nervous as those playing instruments on stage.

'A lot of skills are needed for the job. You have to make sure you don't turn two pages at once and make sure you find the repeats in the music when you have to go back to the right spot,' Mr Titterman explained.

Being a page turner requires plenty of practice. Some pieces of music can go for 40 minutes and require up to 50 page turns, including back turns for repeat passages. Silent onstage communication is key, and each pianist has their own style of 'nodding' to indicate a page turn which they need to practise with their page turner.

But like all performances, there are moments when things go wrong. 'I was turning the page to get ready for the next page, but the draft wind from the turn caused the spare pages to fall off the stand,' Mr Titterman said. 'Luckily I was able to catch them and put them back.'

Most page turners are piano students or up-and-coming concert pianists, although Ms Raspopova has once asked her husband to help her out on stage.

'My husband is the worst page turner,' she laughed. 'He's absorbed in the music, feeling every note, and I have to say: "Turn, turn!" Robert is the best page turner I've had in my entire life.'
Which of the following best describes Titterman's job on stage?

'A lot of skills are needed for the job. You have to make sure you don't turn two pages at once and make sure you find the repeats in the music when you have to go back to the right spot,' Mr Titterman explained.

Being a page turner requires plenty of practice. Some pieces of music can go for 40 minutes and require up to 50 page turns, including back turns for repeat passages. Silent onstage communication is key, and each pianist has their own style of 'nodding' to indicate a page turn which they need to practise with their page turner.

But like all performances, there are moments when things go wrong. 'I was turning the page to get ready for the next page, but the draft wind from the turn caused the spare pages to fall off the stand,' Mr Titterman said. 'Luckily I was able to catch them and put them back.'

Most page turners are piano students or up-and-coming concert pianists, although Ms Raspopova has once asked her husband to help her out on stage.

'My husband is the worst page turner,' she laughed. 'He's absorbed in the music, feeling every note, and I have to say: "Turn, turn!" Robert is the best page turner I've had in my entire life.'
What was a cause of the waterfowl population decline in North America?
考点：细节理解。首段“Millions of acres of wetlands were dried...greatly reducing waterfowl habitat”，湿地被排干使栖息地锐减，A 对。B、C 原文未提，D 与“猎手和移民是人为原因”相悖。

When the explorers first set foot upon the continent of North America, the skies and lands were alive with an astonishing variety of wildlife. Native Americans had taken care of these precious natural resources wisely. Unfortunately, it took the explorers and the settlers who followed only a few decades to decimate a large part of these resources. Millions of waterfowl were killed at the hands of market hunters and a handful of overly ambitious sportsmen. Millions of acres of wetlands were dried to feed and house the ever-increasing populations, greatly reducing waterfowl habitat.

In 1934, with the passage of the Migratory Bird Hunting Stamp Act (Act), an increasingly concerned nation took firm action to stop the destruction of migratory waterfowl and the wetlands so vital to their survival. Under this Act, all waterfowl hunters 16 years of age and over must annually purchase and carry a Federal Duck Stamp. The very first Federal Duck Stamp was designed by J. N. 'Ding' Darling, a political cartoonist from Des Moines, Iowa, who at that time was appointed by President Franklin Roosevelt as Director of the Bureau of Biological Survey. Hunters willingly pay the stamp price to ensure the survival of our natural resources.

About 98 cents of every duck stamp dollar goes directly into the Migratory Bird Conservation Fund to purchase wetlands and wildlife habitat for inclusion into the National Wildlife Refuge System — a fact that ensures this land will be protected and available for all generations to come. Since 1934, better than half a billion dollars has gone into that Fund to purchase more than 5 million acres of habitat. Little wonder the Federal Duck Stamp Program has been called one of the most successful conservation programs ever initiated.

What is a common misunderstanding of emotional intelligence?
It can be measured by an IQ test.
It helps to exercise a person's mind.
It includes a set of emotional skills.
It refers to a person's positive qualities.
考点：细节理解。首段“misunderstand emotional intelligence as almost everything desirable in a person's makeup”，即把情商等同于一切好品质，D 对。A 与“无法用智商测试衡量”相反，C 是作者主张的正确理解而非误解，B 原文未提。

Popularization has in some cases changed the original meaning of emotional intelligence. Many people now misunderstand emotional intelligence as almost everything desirable in a person's makeup that cannot be measured by an IQ test, such as character, motivation, confidence, mental stability, optimism and 'people skills.' Research has shown that emotional skills may contribute to some of these qualities, but most of them move far beyond skill-based emotional intelligence.

We prefer to describe emotional intelligence as a specific set of skills that can be used for either good or bad purposes. The ability to accurately understand how others are feeling may be used by a doctor to find how best to help her patients, while a cheater might use it to control potential victims. Being emotionally intelligent does not necessarily make one a moral person.

Although popular beliefs regarding emotional intelligence run far ahead of what research can reasonably support, the overall effects of the publicity have been more beneficial than harmful. The most positive aspect of this popularization is a new and much needed emphasis on emotion by employers, educators and others interested in promoting social well-being. The popularization of emotional intelligence has helped both the public and researchers re-evaluate the functionality of emotions and how they serve people adaptively in everyday life.

Although the continuing popular appeal of emotional intelligence is desirable, we hope that such attention will excite a greater interest in the scientific and scholarly study of emotion. It is our hope that in coming decades, advances in science will offer new perspectives from which to study how people manage their lives. Emotional intelligence, with its focus on both head and heart, may serve to point us in the right direction.

My husband and I just spent a week in Paris. (36) So the first thing we did was rent a fantastically expensive sixth-floor apartment the size of a cupboard. It was so tiny that we had to leave our suitcases in the hallway.

The place wasn't entirely authentic, though. Unlike a normal Parisian apartment, the plumbing worked. (37) Our building even had a tiny lift with a female voice that said, "Ouverture des portes," in perfect French. That is the only French phrase I mastered, and it's a shame I don't have much use for it.

Parisians are different from you and me. They never look lazy or untidy. As someone noted in this paper a couple of weeks ago, they eat great food and never gain weight. (38) French strawberries do not taste like cardboard. Instead, they explode in your mouth like little flavor bombs.

(39) On our first morning in Paris, I went around the corner to the food market to pick up some groceries. I bought a handful of perfectly ripe small strawberries and a little sweet melon. My husband and I agreed they were the best fruit we had ever eaten. But they cost $18!

In France, quality of life is much more important than efficiency. You can tell this by café life. French cafés are always crowded. (40) When do these people work? The French take their 35-hour workweek seriously — so seriously that some labor unions recently struck a deal with a group of companies limiting the number of hours that independent contractors can be on call.

Children's Discovery Museum

General Information about Group Play

Pricing

Group Play $7/person

Scholarships

We offer scholarships to low-income schools and youth organizations, subject to availability. Participation in a post-visit survey is required.

Scholarships are for Group Play admission fees and/or transportation. Transportation invoices (发票) must be received within 60 days of your visit to guarantee the scholarship.

Group Size

We require one chaperone (监护人) per ten children. Failure to provide enough chaperones will result in an extra charge of $50 per absent adult.

Group Play is for groups of 10 or more with a limit of 35 people. For groups of 35 or more, please call to discuss options.

Hours

The Museum is open daily from 9:30 am to 4:30 pm.

Group Play may be scheduled during any day or time the Museum is open.

Registration Policy

Registration must be made at least two weeks in advance.

Register online or fill out a Group Play Registration Form with multiple date and start time options.

Once the registration form is received and processed, we will send a confirmation email within two business days.

Guidelines

• Teachers and chaperones should model good behavior for the group and remain with students at all times.

• Children are not allowed unaccompanied in all areas of the Museum.

• Children should play nicely with each other and exhibits.

• Use your indoor voice when at the Museum.

We journalists live in a new age of storytelling, with many new multimedia tools. Many young people don't even realize it's new. For them, it's just normal.

This hit home for me as I was sitting with my 2-year-old grandson on a sofa over the Spring Festival holiday. I had brought a children's book to read. It had simple words and colorful pictures — a perfect match for his age.

Picture this: my grandson sitting on my lap as I hold the book in front so he can see the pictures. As I read, he reaches out and pokes (戳) the page with his finger.

What's up with that? He just likes the pictures, I thought. Then I turned the page and continued. He poked the page even harder. I nearly dropped the book. I was confused: Is there something wrong with this kid?

Sorry, kid. This book is not part of your high-tech world. It's an outdated, lifeless thing. An antique. Like your grandfather. Well, I may be old, but I'm not hopelessly challenged, digitally speaking. I edit video and produce audio. I use mobile payment. I've even built websites.

There's one notable gap in my new-media experience, however: I've spent little time in front of a camera, since I have a face made for radio. But that didn't stop China Daily from asking me last week to share a personal story for a video project about the integration of Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei province.

Why did the kid poke the storybook?

He was angry with his grandpa.
He wanted to read it by himself.

Over the last seven years, most states have banned texting by drivers, and public service campaigns have tried a wide range of methods to persuade people to put down their phones when they are behind the wheel.

Yet the problem, by just about any measure, appears to be getting worse. Americans are still texting while driving, as well as using social networks and taking photos. Road accidents, which had fallen for years, are now rising sharply.

That is partly because people are driving more, but Mark Rosekind, the chief of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, said distracted (分心) driving was “only increasing, unfortunately.”

“Big change requires big ideas,” he said in a speech last month, referring broadly to the need to improve road safety. So to try to change a distinctly modern behavior, lawmakers and public health experts are reaching back to an old approach: They want to treat distracted driving like drunk driving.

An idea from lawmakers in New York is to give police officers a new device called the Textalyzer. It would work like this: An officer arriving at the scene of a crash could ask for the phones of the drivers and use the Textalyzer to check in the operating system for recent activity. The technology could determine whether a driver had just texted, emailed or done anything else that is not allowed under New York's hands-free driving laws.

“We need something on the books that can change people's behavior,” said Félix W. Ortiz, who pushed for the state's 2001 ban on hand-held devices by drivers. “If the Textalyzer bill becomes law,” he said, “people are going to be more afraid to put their hands on the cell phone.”

写作意图题。橡皮筋久放抽屉会变干、易断，喻指心脏随年龄增长逐渐失去弹性，与首段“心脏处理氧气效率下降、五十多岁出现迹象”呼应，故选 D。A 项谈锻炼方法、B 项谈病因、C 项谈健身难度，都不是比喻的落点。

As we age, even if we're healthy, the heart just isn't as efficient in processing oxygen as it used to be. In most people the first signs show up in their 50s or early 60s. And among people who don't exercise, the changes can start even sooner.

“Think of a rubber band. In the beginning, it is flexible, but put it in a drawer for 20 years and it will become dry and easily broken,” says Dr. Ben Levine, a heart specialist at the University of Texas. That's what happens to the heart. Fortunately for those in midlife, Levine is finding that even if you haven't been an enthusiastic exerciser, getting in shape now may help improve your aging heart.

Levine and his research team selected volunteers aged between 45 and 64 who did not exercise much but were otherwise healthy. Participants were randomly divided into two groups. The first group participated in a program of nonaerobic (无氧) exercise — balance training and weight training — three times a week. The second group did high-intensity aerobic exercise under the guidance of a trainer for four or more days a week. After two years, the second group saw remarkable improvements in heart health.

“We took these 50-year-old hearts and turned the clock back to 30- or 35-year-old hearts,” says Levine. “And the reason they got so much stronger and fitter was that their hearts could now fill a lot better and pump (泵送) a lot more blood during exercise.” But the hearts of those who participated in less intense exercise didn't change, he says.

“The sweet spot in life to start exercising, if you haven't already, is in late middle age when the heart still has flexibility,” Levine says. “We put healthy 70-year-olds through a yearlong exercise training program, and nothing happened to them at all.”

Dr. Nieca Goldberg, a spokeswoman for the American Heart Association, says Levine's findings are a great start. But the study was small and needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people to determine exactly which aspects of an exercise routine make the biggest difference.
In which aspect were the two groups different in terms of research design?
细节题。第三段写明第一组做无氧的平衡训练和力量训练，第二组做高强度有氧运动，差别在运动类型，选 C。文中说志愿者“其他方面健康”、条件相当，D 项排除；A、B 项文中根本没有提及。

Writing an essay is a difficult process for most people. However, the process can be made easier if you learn to practice three simple techniques.

(36) When you are first trying to think of ideas for an essay, put your pen to your paper and write nonstop for ten or fifteen minutes without letting your pen leave the paper. Stay loose and free. (37) Don't worry about grammar or spelling. Even though this technique won't work for everyone, it helps many people get a good store of ideas to draw on.

The next technique is to write your draft rapidly without worrying about being perfect. (38) Yet, by learning to live with imperfection, you will save yourself headaches and a wastepaper basket full of crumpled (揉皱的) paper. Think of your first draft as a path cut out of the jungle as part of an exploration, not as a complete highway.

The third technique is to try printing out a triple-spaced (三倍行距) copy to allow space for revision. (39) As a result, these writers never get in the habit of crossing out chunks (大块) of their draft and writing revisions in the blank space. After you have revised your draft until it is too messy to work from anymore, you can enter your changes into your word processor. (40) The resulting blank space invites you to revise.

(36) When you are first trying to think of ideas for an essay, put your pen to your paper and write nonstop for ten or fifteen minutes without letting your pen leave the paper. Stay loose and free. (37) Don't worry about grammar or spelling. Even though this technique won't work for everyone, it helps many people get a good store of ideas to draw on.

The next technique is to write your draft rapidly without worrying about being perfect. (38) Yet, by learning to live with imperfection, you will save yourself headaches and a wastepaper basket full of crumpled (揉皱的) paper. Think of your first draft as a path cut out of the jungle as part of an exploration, not as a complete highway.

The third technique is to try printing out a triple-spaced (三倍行距) copy to allow space for revision. (39) As a result, these writers never get in the habit of crossing out chunks (大块) of their draft and writing revisions in the blank space. After you have revised your draft until it is too messy to work from anymore, you can enter your changes into your word processor. (40) The resulting blank space invites you to revise.
